functions.name: DDSTextureSurfaceHierarchyBuild
functions.summary: Parses a DDS buffer and builds a linked-list surface hierarchy for a mip-mapped and/or cubemap texture. Validates the buffer length (a3 >= 4, then a3-4 >= 0x7C), the DDS magic 542327876, and the pixel-format flags (dword at a2+112 masked by 0xFC00 must be 64512 for 6 cubemap faces, 0 for 1 face, else failure). Copies header fields into the root surface object (this+0xC, this+0x10, this+0x14) and searches the pixel-format table rooted at dword_5D71F8 (9-dword entries) for a matching format. For each face and each mip level it allocates an 84-byte surface sub-object via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, initializes it via F_7FieldInitializer, computes row stride and size from the format and current width/height, advances the data pointer and halving width/height per mip. Returns 0 on success, -2147467259 on format/length failure and -2147024882 on allocation failure.

operations.description: If the DDS buffer length a3 is less than 4, return -2147467259.
If the first dword of the buffer does not equal 542327876 (the DDS magic), return -2147467259.
If the remaining header length a3-4 is less than 0x7C, return -2147467259.

Copy DDS header fields into the root object: this+0xC receives the dword at a2+16, this+0x10 receives the dword at a2+12, and this+0x14 receives 1 when the signed byte at a2+10 is non-negative else the mip-count dword at a2+24, clamped to at least 1.
Evaluate pixel-format flags: mask the dword at a2+112 with 0xFC00; 64512 selects 6 faces (cubemap), zero selects 1 face, and any other masked value returns -2147467259.
Read the depth/mip count from the dword at a2+28, defaulting to 1 when it is zero.
Walk the pixel-format table rooted at dword_5D71F8 in 9-dword entries, matching the entry whose pixel size at a2+76 is 32 and whose flag-mask comparisons at a2+80 through a2+104 succeed.
Look up the format descriptor via IDToStructTableLookup and set the root type field this+0x44 to 2*(face_count==6)+3, or 4 when the format descriptor's second dword differs from 1.
If the remaining buffer length is at least 0x400 (1024 bytes), consume 1024 bytes and continue building from the data region at a2+1152 with a2+128 as the base offset.

For each face and each mip level, allocate an 84-byte surface sub-object via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and initialize it via F_7FieldInitializer; compute the row stride from the format (block-compressed formats use 16*((width+3)>>2) or 4*((width+1)>>1), others width*(bytes_per_pixel>>3)) and the size as stride times height (block-aligned height for block formats); halve width, height and bytes-per-pixel for each successive mip level.

Initialize each surface object's fields: format id at offset 0x0, data pointer at 0x4, base/data-region link at 0x8, width at 0xC, height at 0x10, bytes-per-pixel/depth at 0x14, row stride at 0x30, surface size at 0x34, and zeroed flags at 0x38 and 0x3C.
If the remaining buffer is smaller than the computed surface size, return -2147467259; if an 84-byte sub-object allocation fails, return -2147024882.
Return 0 once every face and mip surface is built.
